reason: 'her uncle, who installed them [wind turbines], call the job a sinecure compared with the refinery work... safe and indoor and dull.' Installing wind turbines is outdoor work at height, not a safe indoor job; the story presents this uncorrected.

'It compiles. Everything runs.' / 'The screen said null.' With 'public void Book(String t)' the class has no constructor taking a String, so 'new Book("Persuasion")' fails to compile; it would not run and print null.
'Nineteen feet four inches.' ... 'That's half a foot of margin of error.' A 22-foot prediction against a 19 ft 4 in landing is a 2 ft 8 in gap, not half a foot; the error is never corrected.

'thirty years after publishing those volumes, Thiers had signed off on shooting Parisians in the streets.' The History appeared 1823-1827 and Thiers crushed the Commune in 1871, about 44 years later (the rue Transnonain killings were 1834); source: Wikipedia, Adolphe Thiers.

'a lopsided triangle, sliced it into floors, and labeled them from bottom to top: exposition, rising action, climax, falling action, resolution' (resolution then called 'that last narrow floor'). In Freytag's pyramid the climax is the apex, and falling action and resolution come down the other side; source: Wikipedia, Dramatic structure.

'the official answer: twelve meters... launch speed twelve point four', and then 'Air' explains the ball landing farther than the recalculation. At 12.4 m/s and 30 degrees the vacuum range is about 13.6 m, not 12 m, and air resistance shortens a flight; it cannot make a ball go farther than the prediction.

'He asked the youngest the four questions as tradition required.' By tradition the youngest child asks the Four Questions (Wikipedia, Four Questions). Also 'sundown was around 7:40, which gave him two hours and forty minutes in the small room before the Bernsteins needed the lobby' is wrong arithmetic: 5:00 to the 8:00 booking is three hours; 2h40 is only the time until sundown.

'The answer unfolded along the cold blue to warm pink line the demo had shown.' In the cobalt chloride equilibrium the solution is pink when cold and blue when hot (NCSSM and Temple chem-demo notes). The equation is also misnamed: 'CoCl6' is not a species in it; it is [Co(H2O)6]2+ against [CoCl4]2-.
'She checked the arithmetic twice, dividing 585 by 58.44, and got 10.006.' 585 / 58.44 = 10.010, not 10.006.

'...the desert horizon, the coral band of the dress.' In The Broken Column, Kahlo wears no dress. She is nude except for a white corset and a sheet wrapped around her lower body (Wikipedia, The Broken Column). The injected fact about the nails, tears and direct gaze is stated correctly.

'Minus 18 degrees Celsius on average, the narrator said' about the Moon, and 'the Earth did, at minus 18, before the blanket.' The Moon's mean temperature is far colder (about -60 C at the equator per Diviner, UCLA), and -18 C is a hypothetical Earth with no greenhouse effect, not an actual past state of Earth. The injected -18/14 fact itself is stated correctly.

'The Second Sex, Simone de Beauvoir, the translation dated 1949 on the copyright page.' The book was published in French in 1949; the first English translation (Parshley) came out in 1953 (MIT Libraries 150 Books). The quotation and the 1949 original publication are otherwise correct.
'She began to drift left... Madison looked over her right shoulder.' When moving left to merge, the driver must check the blind spot over the left shoulder, not the right.
'the F on the top space of the treble staff where it belonged.' The top space of the treble staff is E; F (F5) sits on the top line.

'thirty-five and thirty-four sitting side by side... the one vote... between them.' The Senate voted 35 to convict when 36 were needed (35-19); 34 has no role, and the one-vote gap is between 35 and 36 (Wikipedia, Impeachment trial of Andrew Johnson).

'got one that said GGU, arginine. She walked the ribbon until she found GCC.' GGU codes glycine, GCC codes alanine, and GGU does not pair with GCC; the AUG card also 'matches' the AUG codon identically, whereas an anticodon is complementary (UAC). Also 'They're turgid' describes wilted, soft seedlings; turgid means swollen and firm.

'The sky was torn open by fissures the same pale grey as the column.' In The Broken Column the fissures are in the arid, cracked ground; the sky is stormy, not fissured (Wikipedia, The Broken Column).

The story has (low + high) / 2 overflow on a 200-million-element array. With 32-bit ints, low + high stays under about 400 million, far below 2,147,483,647; overflow needs arrays of more than about 1.07 billion elements.

'Carlyle wrote as if... a "dread chasseur" hunting France toward doom.' The quoted phrase does not appear in Carlyle's The French Revolution (Project Gutenberg full text checked); it is a quotation invented and attributed to him.

The story has Annabelle eat rice and chicken that 'sat at the back of the fridge... for five days' after reheating it to 165 F, as if reheating solves the question of age. USDA says to keep leftovers in the fridge for only 3-4 days (usda.gov leftovers guidance), and reheating does not make older leftovers safe.

The story says 36 g of hydrogen reacting with oxygen gives 'Eighteen grams' of water. 36 g H2 is 18 mol, which gives 18 mol H2O, or 324 g of water. The mole method the story teaches gives 324 g, not 18 g.

The story presents cooking the week's chicken and rice on the weekend and eating it from the fridge through 'Friday's dinner' as a working plan. USDA says cooked leftovers keep 3-4 days in the refrigerator (usda.gov leftovers guidance). Anything for later in the week should be frozen.

'the maid who packed Jane's trunk in the middle of the crisis, working while Jane wept' (and the mother's 'The maid packing while Jane stands there'). In Jane Eyre, Jane's trunks were already packed and corded before the wedding (ch. 25). She leaves them behind and flees with only a small parcel (ch. 27; Rochester later says 'your trunks were left corded and locked'). Source: Project Gutenberg text #1260.

'blocked on the thrust stage in the main house, with the audience in a single dark wedge facing the action' / 'composing for a single viewpoint'. A thrust stage has the audience on three sides (Wikipedia, Thrust stage); a single facing audience describes a proscenium stage.

'She ran the letters again from the beginning. Serine, histidine, glycine, leucine.' Read from the first letter, UCC AUG GGA CUU decodes as serine, methionine, glycine, leucine; there is no CAU (histidine) or GGG codon in that frame.

'the red of the lower half and the blood at the corners of her mouth' / 'the corset is grey because her actual corset was grey'. In The Broken Column her lower body is wrapped in a white sheet, the corset straps are white, and there is no blood at her mouth, only tears (NYU Medical Humanities, medhum.med.nyu.edu/view/12902).

'a single person deciding, on a Thursday in March, to walk through a particular door and press a particular button.' 28 March 1979 was a Wednesday, and Commons divisions are counted by MPs walking through lobbies, not by pressing buttons.

'two moles of water for every mole of oxygen'. In CH4 + 2O2 -> CO2 + 2H2O there is one mole of water per mole of O2 (5.0 g O2 = 0.156 mol gives 0.156 mol H2O). Also 'how many sandwiches... Two... Right.': two slices of bread make one sandwich, so the limiting-reactant analogy is miscounted.

'Fourteen names had NULL beside them, and at the top... was Mr. Halloran.' Halloran has an order (the 1998 plum tree), so a Customers LEFT JOIN Orders returns that order row for him, not NULL; NULL only appears for customers with no orders at all.
'Isabelle marries Heathcliff to escape her brother's control'. The character in Wuthering Heights is Isabella Linton, not Isabelle.

'the aluminum frame that had been bent so many times by deliveries that it had gone ductile, soft at the corner'. Repeated bending work-hardens and fatigues aluminum, making it less ductile, not more.

'monthly carbon dioxide measurements from a station on a volcano in Hawaii called Mauna Loa, marching across a century.' The Mauna Loa record only began in March 1958, so it spans under 70 years, not a century (Wikipedia, Keeling Curve).
'watching twelve twelve-year-olds... Coach Reyes, who had handed her the mites' Mites are the 8-and-under division in USA Hockey; twelve-year-olds play Peewee (Wikipedia, Minor ice hockey).

'Keira drew petitioner, the student's side' and the unanswered 'Schools aren't Congress. So how does it even apply?' In the real banner case (Morse v. Frederick) the school principal was the petitioner, and the First Amendment has applied to public-school students since Tinker (1969), so the story wrongly treats that as an open question (Wikipedia, Morse v. Frederick; Tinker v. Des Moines).

The worked example is impossible: a cubic with f(0)=2, f(6)=11 and a critical point at 3.5 with value 4 has f''(3.5)>0, so the 'second derivative' could not show 'a peak and not a valley.' No cubic has a local maximum of 4 at x=3.5 with those endpoint values (recomputed).

'Black, wings folded, hanging dead from the thorn necklace', 'crowded with monkey faces', plus a butterfly at lower left and 'a single fuchsia ribbon' on her forehead. In the painting the hummingbird's wings are outstretched, there is one monkey, and the butterflies are clips in her hair; there is no forehead ribbon (Wikipedia, Self-Portrait with Thorn Necklace and Hummingbird).

'He swapped the two values, ran the test again, and watched the bar turn green.' Swapping assertEquals arguments only changes the failure message; it cannot turn a failing equality check into a passing one. The fact itself is stated correctly.

'She wrote the signs in like weather reports, plus, plus, minus' The derivative is positive below 4, negative between 4 and 11 and positive above 11, so the sign chart is plus, minus, plus, which the story itself gives later.

'between "vermilion" and "vernal," sat her grandfather's word, which turned out to be "vertigo."' Alphabetically, vertigo comes after vernal, not between vermilion and vernal. Also, six halvings of a roughly 1,000-page dictionary leave about 16 pages, not 'a single page'.
'128 over 76... The first reading was fine, under both thresholds.' Under the same 2017 ACC/AHA guideline, 120-129 over less than 80 is 'elevated', not normal (Wikipedia, Blood pressure).

'You did the complement backwards. You just wrote the same letters in reverse order' CTAATGT is the correct base-pair complement of GATTACA, not its reverse, so only the T's needed to become U's (CUAAUGU). Also, 'The fourth one. In DNA it's an A' is wrong: the fourth base of GATTACA is T.

'the laundromat unit, nine hundred and ninety if heat and water together came in under a hundred and forty' The laundromat rent is $890 ($60 less than $950), so a $990 total means $100 of utilities, not 'under $140'; the story's worked total does not add up (and leaves out hydro, which that lease also excludes).

'it's hilarious because he doesn't clock that they're con men for the longest time.' In Chapter 19 Huck says 'It didn't take me long to make up my mind that these liars warn't no kings nor dukes at all, but just low-down humbugs and frauds'; he sees through them almost at once and keeps quiet (text checked via search of Ch. 19, storgy.com/Goodreads quotations).

'The problem arrived at measure 194. Her recapitulation bracket closed there... Twelve more measures' In Mozart's K. 332 first movement the recapitulation starts at m. 133 and restates the whole 93-bar exposition in the tonic (Wikipedia, Piano Sonata No. 12), so it cannot end at m. 194 with a 12-bar coda to follow.
'the American arrangement: a president elected directly' The US president is chosen indirectly, by the Electoral College (Article II and the 12th Amendment), not by direct popular vote.
'This is most of it. This one can.' The can holds 890 mg x 2.5 servings = 2,225 mg (about 2.2 g) of sodium, which is more than the whole 2 g WHO daily limit, not 'most of it'.

'So the list was broken before, with the four names, and broken after, with none.' 'Right.' The same NOT IN query on the same data with the NULL present cannot return four names on Tuesday and zero rows later; with a NULL in the list NOT IN always returns nothing, so the NULL could not have caused the four wrong names. The injected fact itself is stated correctly.

'let the smear sit thirty seconds. It set dull and streaked' / 'the smear set in fifteen seconds with a shine'. A tempered test smear takes roughly 2-5 minutes to set at room temperature, and untempered chocolate does not set (or show bloom) within 30 seconds (King Arthur Baking tempering guide). Also 'It bends instead' overstates compound chocolate's weaker snap.

'The exposition she could feel closing around bar ninety-three' and the development fragment 'in the middle of the storm, bar one hundred and six'. In K. 333/I the exposition ends at bar 63, the development runs about bars 64-93 and the recapitulation begins at bar 93/94, so bar 106 is in the recapitulation (Pearson Edexcel A-level K. 333 analysis, found via search).

'She counted the key signature on the page. E-flat major.' A C minor movement already carries a three-flat key signature, the same as E-flat major, so counting the key signature cannot show the second theme is in E-flat; the key is identified from the harmony and accidentals.

'Thirty-eight, again ... thirty-eight was what his own arithmetic kept insisting' while he counted the citric acid cycle only once. Counting one turn per glucose loses the second turn's ATP, 3 NADH and FADH2 (about 12 ATP in the 38 accounting), so the one-turn total cannot come out at 36 or 38; the story's worked count is wrong.

The empty bag reads 'Twenty-six grams', then Emma adds magnesium ribbon and powder and 'The needle didn't move. Twenty-six grams, sealed.' Adding material to the bag must increase its mass; conservation of mass means mass is unchanged by the reaction, not by adding reactants.

'I had cast Dev as Filer, the complainer' in Pinter's 'Trouble in the Works'. The sketch's two characters are Mr Fibbs (the boss) and Wills (the works man reporting the complaints); there is no Filer (Wikipedia, Trouble in the Works).

'Eight hundred against five weeks of five hundred and forty came in just under. Flat B was legal.' At 540 pounds a month, five weeks' rent is about 623 pounds (540 x 12 / 52 x 5), so an 800-pound deposit is over the cap and Flat B's deposit is not legal either.

'Rambam says cruelty.' In Guide for the Perplexed III:48 Maimonides explains the meat-and-milk ban as gross, over-filling food probably linked to idolatrous festival practice, not cruelty; the cruelty/compassion reading comes from other commentators (Guide III:48, via Sefaria source sheet).

'Forty-five degrees down to eighty-one, seed, hold' and dipping at 'eighty-two. Close enough to hold.' This mixes Celsius and Fahrenheit, and 81-82 F (27-28 C) is the cooling point; tempered dark chocolate is rewarmed to and worked at about 31-32 C (88-90 F) (popsci.com / foodnetwork.com tempering guides).

'They got to the maror later, after the Hillel sandwich.' In the seder, maror is eaten on its own first and korech (the Hillel sandwich) comes right after it (myjewishlearning.com, 14 steps of the seder). Also, horseradish is the answer given to 'what is that green stuff', but horseradish is not green.

The story places the end of the first theme and the start of the busy transition at m. 22 of K. 333, but the transition runs mm. 11-22 and the second theme begins at m. 23 in F major. It also says K. 309's second theme comes back 'in the same key as the first, no new key at all', but in K. 309 the second theme is in G major, the dominant (Unisa K. 309 analysis; K. 333 analyses).

'Her first attempt gave her a field of almost a trillion volts per metre... she had multiplied by the constant instead of dividing.' Multiplying the charge density by 8.85e-12 gives a far smaller number than dividing, not a larger one; the described error could not produce a trillion V/m.

'the warm-up would take the first ten minutes... It's called the FIFA 11 plus' and 'Nine of us here, that's like three fewer seasons ending on a stretcher.' The 11+ used in the 2008 Norwegian trial is a roughly 20-minute programme (Soligard et al., BMJ 2008), and a one-third cut in injury rate does not mean three of nine players spared.

'the two gases inside had settled into their balanced state, half one compound and half the other.' Equilibrium means the forward and reverse rates are equal, not that the amounts are equal; the NO2/N2O4 mixture is not half and half.

'a pyramid, wide at the base, narrowing to a thread at the top, with the label Japan beneath it... more like a barrel... for Niger.' This is reversed: Niger, with very high fertility, has the wide-based pyramid, and Japan's is barrel-shaped or top-heavy.

'Kennan wires Moscow, says the Soviets are expansionist.' Kennan sent the Long Telegram from the US embassy in Moscow to the State Department in Washington (Feb. 22, 1946; CFR/teachingamericanhistory.org).
'The novel was "The Tell-Tale Heart," all fourteen pages of it.' 'The Tell-Tale Heart' is a short story, not a novel, and it runs only a few pages.

The story has Passover listed on Friday the fifteenth and a Seder on Thursday evening. The Jewish calendar never puts the first day of Passover on a Monday, Wednesday or Friday (the 'lo BaDU Pesach' rule; jhom.com, Chabad), so a Thursday-evening first Seder cannot happen.

'She had written void in front of it... the compiler had never complained' while the tester printed 0.0, then deleting void gave 250.0. With only a void method Account(String,double), Java supplies just a no-arg constructor, so a tester passing the owner and 250 would not compile; one calling new Account() would stop compiling once the real constructor is added. The shown before/after sequence is impossible Java.

'adding up her rectangles again, all thirty of them, and getting 8.8275.' For y = x^2 on [0,3] with 30 rectangles the left sum is 8.555, the right sum 9.455 and the midpoint sum 8.9975; none gives 8.8275.

'It's not ritual. It's not about the temple. It's sandwiched between laws about theft and lying.' Leviticus 19:9-10 is preceded by 19:5-8 on sacrifices of well-being (ritual law) and followed by 19:11 on stealing and lying (BibleGateway, NRSVUE).
'The feminist sheet said Charlotte Bronte had to publish under a man's name' about Wuthering Heights. Wuthering Heights is by Emily Bronte, published as Ellis Bell (Wikipedia, Wuthering Heights).

'The white dress is this kind of impermeable surface, nothing gets in, blood goes everywhere else but the dress stays white.' In The Two Fridas blood from the vessel cut by the forceps spills onto the European Frida's white dress (Wikipedia, The Two Fridas); she also holds forceps, not scissors.

'She was sixteen, three years too young to vote.' That implies a voting age of 19, which no country uses; the voting age in the UK and Canada (the setting's spelling and polling terms) is 18 (Wikipedia, Voting age).
'The graph was the Mauna Loa carbon dioxide record, a century squashed into one axis.' The Mauna Loa record began in March 1958, so it covers under 70 years, not a century (Wikipedia, Keeling Curve).

The learner practises merging onto a motorway at seventy miles an hour with her grandmother before passing her test, and the story treats this as fine. Under Highway Code rule 253 (gov.uk), a learner on a GB motorway must be with an approved driving instructor in a dual-control car.

'Even, the review implied, when the positive ones outnumbered them five to one.' The 2001 Baumeister review (citing Gottman) says good interactions must outnumber bad ones by at least five to one for the good to prevail, not that bad still wins at five to one (checked in the review's text).

'He said the tradition calls the broader obligation a fence, a fence around the law.' A 'fence around the Torah' (Pirkei Avot 1:1) means extra rabbinic safeguards against breaking a law. It is not the name for extending the parapet duty to other hazards (Wikipedia, 'Fence around the Torah').

'She had checked the key signature on the score, and there it was, one sharp where there had been none.' In a Mozart C major sonata exposition the key signature does not change. The move to G major is written with accidentals (F sharps), not a new key signature.

'He reversed the two arguments in his assertEquals, ran the test, and watched the bar turn green.' Swapping expected and actual only changes the failure message. assertEquals(14.99, 24.99) fails either way, so the swap cannot make a failing test pass (the girl's test 'Green.' has the same error).

The story places the end of K. 333's second movement development at measure 98 and a retransition around measure 90, with a false recapitulation in the wrong key. That movement is 82 measures long: development mm. 32-50, recapitulation from m. 51 (PTNA piano encyclopedia, enc.piano.or.jp).

The story has the K. 332 Adagio wander through keys in a development before the recapitulation. That movement is in sonatina form with no development section (Wikipedia, 'Piano Sonata No. 12 (Mozart)'); after the double bar the theme returns at once, turning to B-flat minor.

'He says he's tapping Ackley on the shoulder to say goodnight, and then he admits the whole thing was a lie.' No such scene is in the novel; Holden's Ackley scenes (ch. 3, 7) contain no confessed goodnight lie (LitCharts ch. 3 and ch. 7 summaries). The 'terrific liar' line leads into his lie to Mr. Spencer about the gym; the quote and 1951 date are correct.

'She drew a small dot after the half note, then counted: the note, and the dot, one-two-three, and the fourth beat of silence before the next bar began, and the bar was full.' The rhythm maths doesn't add up. The bar was one beat short, so the dot's extra beat should fill it with no leftover silence. And a 4/4 bar holding a three-beat dotted half is only full if a quarter note or quarter rest is written, not an unwritten 'beat of silence'. The injected fact itself is stated correctly.
